scores.evidence: The Japanese uses です・ます throughout. It is warm and free of pressure phrases (s3-b1 「最初から完璧でなくてかまいません。」). The wrong-option feedback names the misunderstanding, then gives the correct idea. A few English lines read as direct translations (s5-b3, q1 option a feedback, q5 option c feedback).

Each segment introduces at most 2 new terms (s1-defs: 壁打ち; s2-defs: 目的・機能; s5-defs: MVP・MoSCoW). lessons:lint --strict reports no sentence-length or paragraph-length findings. One worked example, the budget app, runs through ex-goal to s2-b3.
s1-b1 links back to Chapter 0 (the human's role) and ex-data to the Chapter 1 database. The opening budget-app failure (hook-b1) comes back in s2-table, s5-b2 and the s2-b3 expect example.

Terms match across the glossary, body text and diagram labels (今月の残り画面 and 支出の入力画面 in s2-b4, the text and the s2-b3 expect). The diagram has both alt and description. Notation follows the rules (3つ, 1枚, no spaces). Gaps: 「ビジョン」 appears without English, and a few EN lines are unnatural.

mustFix.issue: The katakana word 「ビジョン」 appears for the first time in this lesson without English. The style guide requires English on first use.
mustFix.fix: 「ビジョンを示すこと」→「ビジョン（vision）を示すこと」

mustFix.issue: The EN sentence is awkward and hard to parse: 'make only the things it couldn't be met without into Musts'.
mustFix.fix: en: "Ask, \"Could the goal still be met without this?\" and make only the things it couldn't be met without into Musts." → "Ask, \"Could the goal still be met without this?\" Only the features the goal can't do without become Musts."

mustFix.issue: The EN feedback for option a reads as a literal translation: 'Questions about features line up features before the goal is set.'
mustFix.fix: en (option a feedback): "Questions about features line up features before the goal is set." → "Asking about features gets you a list of features before the goal is set."

mustFix.issue: The EN feedback for option c is unnatural: 'Asking about features first moves on before the goal is set.'
mustFix.fix: en (option c feedback): "Asking about features first moves on before the goal is set." → "Starting with which features are needed skips past the goal."

niceToHave: glossary MVP: the jp text 「Minimum Viable Product。」 does not match s5-defs 「Minimum Viable Product（実用最小限の製品）の略。」. Use the s5-defs wording in both places.
q2 option a feedback (en): 'it describes a means, showing a table in the app, so it's a feature' would read better as 'what it describes is a means (showing a table in the app), so it's a feature'.
q3 explanation (en): 'A Must is only a feature without which the goal can't be met.' → 'Only features the goal can't do without are Musts.'
q7 and the q3 feedback use 「SNS」 without the full name. It is widely known, but the abbreviation rule asks for it once: 「SNS（ソーシャルメディア）」.
summary-next: 「何でしょう？理由も」 has no space after the full-width ？. A full-width space here (「何でしょう？　理由も」) would match common Japanese typesetting.

Factual check (not changed): q4 explanation says an AI tool maker's guide lists stating what is out of scope as a feature of useful specs. Confirm that the cc-best-practices source actually says this.
summary: The Japanese is natural and warm, and well paced for a phone. The budget-app example and the terms stay consistent from the hook to the one-page plan, and the wrong-option feedback is short and specific throughout. The fixes are small: add English to 「ビジョン」 on its first use and rewrite three translated-sounding English lines (s5-b3, q1, q5).
